review_candidates.description: JOB DESCRIPTION We are hiring Technology Officer. Company: Umerco (Umer & Company) Location: Valencia Town, Lahore (On-site) Job Type: Full-Time, On-site Working Days: Monday to Friday Shift Timings: 6:00 PM – 3:00 AM (PKT) — aligned with USA business hours Experience (8-10 years) Senior ownership of technology, power, and security at our new Lahore office. About Umer & Company Umer & Company (Umerco) is an official IBM partner. We sell IBM products and provide the support and maintenance that goes with them, so our clients get premier solutions at preferred rates along with the expertise to run them properly. Most of our work sits in Managed File Transfer (MFT) and integration, connecting systems and trading partners so businesses spend less time on manual processes and more on the work that matters. We are a young company, and we have set up our Lahore office to support clients through USA business hours. Role Overview We are hiring a senior IT Administrator for our new Lahore office. This is an ownership role. You will decide what the office runs on, keep it running, and answer for it when something breaks. Four things matter most. Power, because load shedding and grid failures are part of working here and our business hours cannot stop when the lights do. Internet stability, because our team works in USA hours and every dropped link is lost time. Hardware and software choices, because what you buy now sets the office up for the next few years. And security and maintenance, done on a schedule rather than after a failure. As the role is senior, it carries more than technical work. You will set standards, guide the support staff, prepare RFPs, deal with vendors and ISPs, and put clear options in front of management. Needs to be proactive to take initiatives for improving the company’s infrastructure and own things from start to finish. Key Responsibilities Technology leadership Own the office technology setup: infrastructure, endpoints, connectivity, power, and physical security. Set the technical standards and write them down, so decisions still hold as the team grows. Guide the support staff, review their escalations, and build their skills over time. Plan the IT roadmap and budget with management, sequencing the work that matters most. Answer for downtime. Nobody should have to ask you to investigate a problem that keeps recurring. Vendors, RFPs, and procurement Write RFPs and RFQs with specifications clear enough that the quotes coming back can be compared fairly. Weigh proposals on capability, total cost, support response, warranty, and whether spares are available locally. Negotiate price, service levels, and support terms, and keep contracts and renewal dates on record. Build relationships with OEMs, local suppliers, and ISPs so faults get attention when you call. Chase issues to closure, escalate when a vendor misses the response time it agreed to, and check that what arrives matches what was ordered. Power and backup Own the backup chain: inverters, UPS units, generator coordination, stabilizers, and transfer switching. Work out how much consumption is needed for office, then size backup capacity and runtime against that figure. Plan around load shedding schedules so business hours run without interruption. Test failover on a schedule and check battery health. An untested backup is not a backup. Set up safe shutdown and startup sequences and protect equipment from voltage swings and earthing faults. Record every power event with its cause and follow it up with vendors or building management. Network and internet stability Look after LAN and Wi-Fi, routers, switches, firewalls, and VPNs. Track faults down quickly, whether they sit in latency, packet loss, DNS, DHCP, routing, or a bad cable. Run more than one internet connection with automatic failover, so one ISP problem does not stop work. Experience with setting up servers, firewalls and switching over exercises Monitor uptime with alerting, so you hear about problems before users report them. Take evidence to the ISP: traceroutes, loss figures, device logs. Escalate with facts, not complaints. Keep call and video quality solid for USA hours work, including QoS for voice traffic. Hardware, software, and provisioning Decide standard specifications for laptops, desktops, servers, monitors, printers, and network gear. Match the specification to the job and the budget, without overbuying or leaving people struggling. Manage assets from purchase through deployment, warranty, refresh, and disposal. Own software and licensing. Keep records accurate and renewals ahead of expiry. Put a written comparison behind any significant purchase, with your recommendation on it. Keep standard builds so new machines go out configured the same way every time. Security and maintenance Administer Microsoft 365 and Active Directory: accounts, groups, permissions, and password policy. Work to a maintenance calendar covering endpoints, network gear, racks, power systems, and cameras, applying patches and antivirus updates on a set cadence. Review access regularly and remove it the day someone leaves. Keep surveillance and access control working and test backups by restoring from them. Keep network diagrams, device configurations, and procedures current enough to use during an incident. Required Qualifications At least 8 years in IT administration or system administration, including 2 years owning an environment or running a small IT function. DAE (CIT or Computer Engineering), BSIT, BSCS, Software Engineering, or a related field. Hands-on experience with inverters, UPS, and generator backed power, including load and runtime calculations. Solid networking: TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, routing, NAT, VPN, firewalls, and Wi-Fi, with practical work on Cisco, MikroTik, UniFi, Huawei, or similar equipment. Good knowledge of Windows 10 and 11, Windows Server, Microsoft 365, and Active Directory. Experience writing RFPs or RFQs, comparing vendor quotes, holding suppliers to service levels, and specifying hardware and software correctly for both the requirement and the budget. Strong spoken and written English, including explaining trade-offs to people outside IT. Leadership. You set direction, bring junior staff along, and stay steady when things go wrong. Willing to work the 6:00 PM to 3:00 AM (PKT) shift on site and respond to outages inside that window. Preferred CCNA, HCIA, CompTIA A+ or Network+, Microsoft certifications, or ITIL Foundation. You have set up a new office from scratch before. Familiarity with IBM hardware or software. Existing contacts among hardware suppliers, ISPs, and service providers in Lahore. Some Linux server administration, plus basic PowerShell or Bash scripting for routine jobs. Monitoring tools such as Zabbix, PRTG, or Uptime Kuma. Structured cabling, patching, and rack installation. How to Apply Direct apply or send your CV at sameen.sajjad@umerco.com

Working knowledge of Microsoft Entra ID, Conditional Access, and device compliance concepts. Familiarity with endpoint security frameworks such as CIS Benchmarks and standard patch management practices.
